quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Use the clutch to shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How important are signals on a motorcycle?

options.text: More important than signals on cars and trucks.
Only needed when another vehicle is right next to you.
Less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: More important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more vulnerable than car and truck drivers. That is why using signals is even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see your turn signals, you should:

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to tell other drivers you are turning.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers what you are doing.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Lean into the slippery area to keep your balance.
Keep your speed up to improve traction.
Not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle straight up and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle straight up and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: Try to avoid slippery roads completely. If you cannot avoid them, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to drive around a train.

questions.question: How often should you check that your headlight and taillight work?
questions.explanation: Always test your lights before you ride. It is very important that they work every time you are on the road.

questions.question: How does snow and ice melt?

options.text: Only when hit by direct sunlight.
At the same rate on all roads.
Faster on some sections of road than others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster on some sections of road than others.
questions.explanation: Snow and ice melt at different rates on different parts of the road. Low areas, shaded areas, bridges, and overpasses stay frozen the longest.

questions.question: What is the benefit of reflective, brightly-colored helmets and clothing?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They help other drivers see you better.
They do not make riding safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help other drivers see you better.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you on the road.

questions.question: What is a sign that your rear tire has gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. You must stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely so they can go by you. Speeding up will only make them tailgate you at higher speeds.

questions.question: Can you ride around lowered gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers go around the gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at any railroad crossing when warning signals appear. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagging person, or train sounds. It is illegal to drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Why should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: You should not wear them because your hands will get too hot.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
You should not wear them because they make the controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of other durable material. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Before riding, check your throttle. When released, it should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your throttle and clutch. The throttle should snap back when you release it, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down. Stop if cars are coming.
Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
Go slowly through the intersection. You do not always need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely. Then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Stop at the marked line. If there is no line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop where you can see oncoming traffic. Then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: Your position in your lane should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Let other drivers share your lane.
Help you see others and let them see you.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and let them see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It keeps other drivers from trying to share your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger occurs.

questions.question: What best reduces the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Downshifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear has the same effect as braking. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chance of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals because it might distract other drivers.
Making sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Making sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To prevent a crash, be visible to other drivers. Signal your intentions clearly. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Look ahead for hazards. Be ready to react to any danger.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning or entering a curve.

questions.question: Orange background signs warn about:
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: Unlike other drinks, alcohol:
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need digestion. It is absorbed directly through the stomach and small intestine walls, enters the bloodstream, and reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: What does this road sign indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs indicate you are in or approaching a school zone or school crossing. Watch for children and follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, you must:
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: You may carry a passenger:

options.text: Only if the passenger is a child.
Only if the passenger has a motorcycle license.
If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: If your motorcycle is designed to carry a passenger.
questions.explanation: You can only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is designed and equipped for it.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only for use if the rear brake fails.

questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used properly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of total stopping power.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from a person's body?
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip of a motorcycle. Learn where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. What should you do?

options.text: Do not ride during the day.
Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a common way to slow down a motorcycle. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on your brake lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns that you are about to reach a divided highway.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing whenever you ride a motorcycle. Crashes happen both during the day and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It is less effective than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When braking, should you only use the rear brake?
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is important when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what is happening both in front and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening both in front and behind you.
questions.explanation: It is most important to watch the road ahead, but you also need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to keep track of traffic behind you.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between your motorcycle and other vehicles so you have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
